data.title: Inovio surges 280% following FDA approval of Voceryq for rare disease
data.description:
• Inovio Pharmaceuticals (INO) is up ~280% in after-hours trading Friday after the US FDA announced it has approved Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) as a treatment for the rare disease recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP).
  • The approval is the first for a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the US.
  • RRP is characterized by small, wart-like growths in the airways. The condition is caused by human papillomavirus.
  • Accelerated approval was granted based on data indicating that Voceryq helped reduce the frequency of surgical procedures needed to remove growths in adults, meeting an intermediate clinical endpoint.
  • Inovio will need to conduct a post-marketing study to confirm the therapy's benefit.
  • The FDA said that the treatment is "designed to stimulate the immune system to respond to and attack cells infected by the specific types of HPV that cause RRP (types 6 and 11)."

data.title: Textron’s unit wins $114.7M Navy contract boost for Marine helicopters
data.description:
• Bell Textron, a subsidiary of Textron (TXT), received a $114.7M U.S. Navy contract modification to upgrade the electrical systems and structures of Marine Corps AH-1Z and UH-1Y helicopters.
  • The award covers 15 A-kits, four mission kits, nine aircraft installations, components, materials, and spare parts.
  • The work is expected to be completed by June 2028.
  • The full $114.7M will be funded through FY2027 Navy aircraft procurement funds.
  • Naval Air Systems Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: Accendra Health gets NYSE non-compliance notice
data.description:
• Accendra Health (ACH) said on Friday that on October 27, 2026, it received a notice from the New York Stock Exchange about non-compliance with the exchange's continued listing standards.
  • The company said it intends to respond to the NYSE within 10 business days of receipt of the notice affirming its intent to submit a business plan.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Annovis Bio gets non-compliance notice from NYSE
data.description:
• Annovis Bio (ANVS) said on Friday that it received a notice regarding non-compliance with the New York Stock Exchange's continued listing standards.
  • According to the notice, as of October 28, 2026, the 30 trading-day average market capitalization of the company was about $48.4M and the last reported stockholders’ deficit as of June 30, 2026, was nearly $4.3M, both below the $50M NYSE threshold.
  • The company said that it has notified the NYSE it will submit a plan within the stipulated timeline on steps it will take to regain compliance.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Standex outlines high single-digit FY 2027 sales growth and high teens adjusted EPS growth, backed by $273M orders
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Standex International (SXI) Q1 2027

Management View

  • "In the fiscal first quarter, we delivered record sales of approximately $233 million, driven by double-digit organic growth" (Chairman, President & CEO David Dunbar). "The Electronics segment led the way with organic growth of nearly 30%" and "record order intake at $273 million and a book-to-bill of 1.17" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • "This gives us confidence to raise our sales outlook for fiscal year 2027" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar). "We now expect total sales to grow high single digits in fiscal 2027, up from our prior outlook calling for mid- to high single-digit growth" and "we expect organic sales to increase by more than $100 million and adjusted earnings per share to grow in the high teens" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • "Earlier this month, we announced the appointment of Samantha Stoddard as our next Chief Financial Officer beginning on December 1" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar). "I want to take a moment to welcome Colby Slaughter as our new Chief Legal Officer" and "I also want to extend a special thanks to Ademir Sarcevic for his contributions as CFO" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • "On a consolidated basis, total revenue increased approximately 7% year-on-year to $232.6 million" (CFO, Executive VP of Corporate & Group President of Electronics Ademir Sarcevic). "First quarter 2027 adjusted operating margin increased 110 basis points year-on-year to 20.2%" and "adjusted earnings per share increased 21.1% year-on-year to $2.41" (CFO Sarcevic).
  • "We achieved several records in the quarter, record organic growth of almost 30%, record bookings and record gross margin" (CFO Sarcevic). "We remain on track to significantly expand global capacity in our grid business" and "we remain very optimistic about the future outlook of this segment" (CFO Sarcevic).

Outlook

  • "We now expect total sales to grow high single digits in fiscal 2027" and "we expect high teens growth in adjusted earnings per share" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • "We still expect to launch more than 20 new products in fiscal 2027" and "we now expect new product sales pro forma for the federal divestiture to grow by $27 million to $94 million" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • "Our sales into the fast-growing markets such as defense, space and grid are now expected to increase more than 20% to greater than $315 million, constituting more than 30% of our total sales" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • "In fiscal second quarter 2027, we expect moderately higher revenue and adjusted operating margin" and "slightly higher revenue and similar adjusted operating margin on a sequential basis" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s fiscal 2027 framework, management changed from "mid- to high single-digit sales growth" to "high single digits" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, current transcript) and kept the multi-year goal: "greater than $1.1 billion in total sales and 23% adjusted operating margin by the end of fiscal year 2028" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, current transcript).

Financial Results

  • "Sales of $232.6 million increased 12.4% organically" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar). "Adjusted gross margin of 44.4% was up 240 basis points year-on-year" and "adjusted operating margin of 20.2% was up 110 basis points year-on-year" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • "Net cash provided by operating activities was $15.7 million" and "we generated fiscal first quarter free cash flow of $9.1 million" (CFO Sarcevic).
  • "Electronics revenue increased 27.1% year-on-year to a record $140.5 million" and "our book-to-bill in fiscal first quarter was 1.23 with record orders of approximately $173 million" (CFO Sarcevic). "Adjusted operating margin of 29.4%" increased "60 basis points year-on-year" (CFO Sarcevic).
  • "Engraving and Hydraulics revenue decreased 14.9% to $40.9 million" (CFO Sarcevic). "Softness in the North American automotive market" was cited as the key driver (CFO Sarcevic).
  • "Our current available liquidity is approximately $168.5 million" and "Standex had net debt of $401.2 million" (CFO Sarcevic). "We declared our 249th consecutive quarterly cash dividend of $0.36 per share" and "in fiscal 2027, we still expect capital expenditures between $45 million and $55 million" (CFO Sarcevic).

Q&A

  • Christopher Moore, CJS Securities, Inc.: asked whether "AI data center build-out" is becoming a larger portion of growth and what happens "if AI growth slows"; Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar: "of the $100 million plus we expect in organic growth this year, it's about 30% of that will come from data centers" and "I wouldn't actually expect this mix to change in the future."
  • Christopher Moore, CJS Securities, Inc.: asked about "long-term supply agreements"; CFO Sarcevic: "we are looking actually to sign in 3- to 5-year long-term agreements with some of our key customers" and "they are very, very interested in actually making sure that we have a capacity to support their growth needs."
  • Christopher Moore, CJS Securities, Inc.: asked what drives the higher end of missile upside; Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar: "I think it will be closer to $20 million this year" and "we think that $40 million to $80 million is likely to be $50 million to $90 million in the coming years."
  • Ross Sparenblek, William Blair & Company L.L.C., Research Division: asked to separate power/grid from legacy electronics; CFO Sarcevic: "the legacy businesses as well as grid were about the same" and "each one of them were over 1.2" (book-to-bill).
  • Ross Sparenblek, William Blair & Company L.L.C., Research Division: asked about Croatia ramp; CFO Sarcevic: "we are now anticipating that we're going to start making actually manufacturing and shipping product out of Croatia within this quarter" and "we're going to see a pretty nice ramp-up there in Q3 and Q4."
  • Matt Koranda, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC, Research Division: asked whether new products include data center exposure; Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar: "There are new products into data centers, but those are included in the data center box to the left."
  • Matt Koranda, ROTH Capital Partners, LLC, Research Division: asked whether the $100 million repurchase signals stepped-up buybacks vs. M&A; Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar: "we announced a new $100 million share repurchase authorization" and "our approach to buybacks has been to be somewhat opportunistic" while "we are still full speed ahead" on capacity expansion and "our funnel is becoming more active" in M&A.
  • Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Research Division: asked what’s driving margin strength; CFO Sarcevic: "it's a combination" of "mix" and "driving productivity" and said the Electronics Edge ERP issues are "on the tail end of that."
  • Gary Prestopino, Barrington Research Associates, Inc., Research Division: asked why corporate expense rose; CFO Sarcevic: "it's up about $3 million year-on-year" driven by "higher variable compensation" and "higher medical costs," plus "a onetime cost" from "executive recruiting and transfers" expected to normalize.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical around concentration and durability of data-center-driven demand, with questions referencing "if AI growth slows" and "all of the noise that's coming out against data centers" (Christopher Moore, CJS; Gary Prestopino, Barrington).
  • Management tone was positive and confident in prepared remarks, emphasizing "confidence to raise our sales outlook" and reiterating long-term targets (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar), while in Q&A it stayed assertive on mix and runway: "I wouldn't actually expect this mix to change" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar) and "orders remain very, very strong" (CFO Sarcevic).
  • Versus the prior quarter, management language moved from expecting fiscal 2027 "mid- to high single-digit sales growth" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, previous transcript) to "high single digits" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, current transcript), and Q&A focus broadened from capacity build mechanics to agreements, international demand, and stock volatility.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance language shifted upward as management moved from "mid- to high single-digit sales growth" for fiscal 2027 (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, previous transcript) to "total sales to grow high single digits" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, current transcript).
  • Electronics growth accelerated in discussion from "Electronics grew 12.9% organically" in Q4 FY 2026 (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, previous transcript) to "Electronics grew 29.5% organically" in Q1 FY 2027 (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, current transcript), alongside continued emphasis on capacity expansion execution.
  • Capital return became more prominent with the new authorization: "a new $100 million share repurchase authorization" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, current transcript), while the previous quarter’s discussion centered more on grid capacity roadmaps and acquisition integration.
  • Leadership updates expanded from an expected legal transition ("I will soon be announcing his replacement" regarding the retiring Chief Legal Officer) (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, previous transcript) to naming the new Chief Legal Officer and incoming CFO timing (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar, current transcript).

Risks and Concerns

  • Management acknowledged demand debates around data centers: "Depending on the country you're in, there is some of the same debate about the impact of data centers on electricity prices, on water, on the local economy" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar), while adding, "we see no change in our expected outlook" (Chairman, President & CEO Dunbar).
  • Execution dependencies cited included customer-controlled timing: "we are at the mercy of their own schedule" for Croatia audits and certifications (CFO Sarcevic), with mitigation framed as phased ramps: "it'll probably be a little bit more linear" as capacity unlocks (CFO Sarcevic).
  • Automotive exposure remained a pressure point: Engraving and Hydraulics weakness reflected "softness in the North American automotive market" (CFO Sarcevic).

Final Takeaway

Standex management framed Q1 FY 2027 as a quarter of record sales and bookings, led by Electronics and supported by new products and fast-growth markets, and used the order backdrop to raise fiscal 2027 sales growth expectations to high single digits while reiterating high-teens adjusted EPS growth. Leadership changes (incoming CFO and new Chief Legal Officer), a new $100 million repurchase authorization, and ongoing grid capacity expansion plans were positioned as supporting the company’s path toward "greater than $1.1 billion" of sales and "23% adjusted operating margin" by the end of fiscal 2028, with management emphasizing that multiple growth drivers—not only data centers—are expected to contribute meaningfully.

data.title: Aptar anticipates Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.39-$1.47 as emergency medicine destocking laps in Q4
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: AptarGroup (ATR) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "I'm pleased to join you today for my first earnings call as CEO of Aptar." (CEO, President & Director Gael Touya)
  • "Our results in the quarter demonstrate the underlying strength of our businesses with 5% core sales growth across all 3 segments and adjusted earnings per share at the higher end of our guidance range." (CEO Touya)
  • "I want to be clear. Sales growth alone is not our objective. Our goal is to convert the strong demand for our products into more consistent profitability." (CEO Touya)
  • "We have excellent technology, strong customer relationships and leading positions in attractive categories. At the same time, the margin performance, mostly in North America is not where it needs to be." (CEO Touya)
  • "We are also expanding our respiratory platform through the acquisition of PULMOTREE, adding its Kolibri non-propellant liquid inhaler technology." (CEO Touya)
  • "We recorded a combined charge of $61.2 million before tax and $60.4 million after tax or $0.94 per diluted share." (Executive VP & CFO Vanessa Kanu)
  • "Our reported sales increased 6% to just over $1 billion and core sales increased 5% compared to the prior year period." (CFO Kanu)
  • "Before I open the call to questions, I wanted to highlight that we recently announced the appointment of Virginie Maes as President of Aptar Pharma effective January 1." (CEO Touya)

Outlook

  • "We anticipate fourth quarter adjusted earnings per share to be in the range of $1.39 to $1.47." (CFO Kanu)
  • "As we look to the remainder of the year, we expect Aptar to finish on a strong note, driven by Pharma." (CEO Touya)
  • "Additionally, the segment will no longer be affected by the emergency medicine destocking headwind." (CEO Touya)
  • "We expect Pharma margins to improve year-over-year as productivity initiatives continue to gain traction and operational efficiencies take hold." (CEO Touya)
  • "For the full year 2026, we continue to expect capital investments to be in the range of $260 million to $280 million and depreciation and amortization expense to be between $310 million and $320 million." (CFO Kanu)
  • "Now turning to our outlook for the fourth quarter" contrasted with the prior quarter’s outlook framing where management said, "Now on to our outlook for Q3." (CFO Kanu, Q2 2026)

Financial Results

  • "Adjusted EBITDA of $217 million" and "an adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.3% compared to 23.2% in the prior year." (CFO Kanu)
  • "Adjusted EPS was $1.52, a decrease of 6% compared to the prior year's adjusted EPS of $1.62 at comparable exchange rates." (CFO Kanu)
  • "Consolidated gross margin declined by 120 basis points year-over-year, primarily due to lower sales of high-margin emergency medicine products and lower gross margins in Beauty and Closures." (CFO Kanu)
  • "Free cash flow year-to-date was $198 million, comprising cash from operations of $390 million, less capital expenditures net of government grants of $192 million." (CFO Kanu)
  • "Over the last 9 months, we have repurchased 1.3 million shares for $180 million." (CFO Kanu)
  • "Additionally, our Board of Directors have authorized an increase in our quarterly dividend by 4%." (CFO Kanu)
  • "As of September 30, we had $420 million remaining under our existing share repurchase authorization." (CFO Kanu)

Q&A

  • Ghansham Panjabi, Baird: "on the emergency medicine destock, is that still tracking in line with plan" and whether there is residual into 2027; CEO Touya: "the destocking impact will be behind us" and "we're going to know this by Q1... 2027." (CEO Touya)
  • Ghansham Panjabi, Baird: asked what drove Pharma margins; CFO Kanu: "we were actually quite pleased to see the 36.4%, higher than the top end of our guidance range" and cited "strong pharma revenues," "Royalties," and "productivity improvements." (CFO Kanu)
  • Paul Knight, KeyBanc: asked if the long-term Pharma growth corridor could move above 11%; CEO Touya: "we are pretty comfortable with that corridor, the 7% and the 11%." (CEO Touya)
  • Matthew Roberts, Raymond James: asked about quarter-to-quarter prescription dynamics and ex-emergency expectations; CEO Touya: "I'm not reading anything specific from quarter-to-quarter with prescription." (CEO Touya)
  • George Staphos, BofA: pressed on what changes under new leadership, particularly for Beauty profitability; CEO Touya: "we have a plan" but "that's not going to be a quick fix" and "that's not going to be a linear improvement." (CEO Touya)
  • Matt Larew, William Blair: asked on Injectables growth and capacity; CEO Touya: "very satisfied with our Injectables business" and "we are not depending on any single blockbuster" and "we like to hit singles or doubles." (CEO Touya)
  • Daniel Rizzo, Jefferies: asked about cough/cold season destocking risk; CEO Touya: "We're going to know that one pretty soon" and highlighted supply chain agility and customer connectivity. (CEO Touya)
  • Justin Bowers, Deutsche Bank: asked about acne Rx-to-OTC timing and naloxone outlook; CEO Touya: "I cannot share the name of the customer" and "GDP plus is our best estimate as of today, and we will get a better understanding by Q1 2027." (CEO Touya)
  • Anojja Shah, UBS: asked whether tariffs pressured North America Beauty margins; CEO Touya: "Not so much" and pointed to "The way we compete... and the way we execute." (CEO Touya)
  • George Staphos, BofA: asked about tax rate drivers and normalization; CFO Kanu: "for Q4 specifically, we're able to... recognize the benefit of some previously unrecognized tax losses" and "21% to 23%" was described as the long-term ETR range. (CFO Kanu)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative on execution and durability, with repeated probing on Beauty underperformance and the post-destocking baseline, including "What's going to change?" (George Staphos, BofA) and questions on margin drivers and seasonality.
  • Management’s tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more measured in Q&A, using explicit caution on pace of improvement: "that's not going to be a quick fix" and "that's not going to be a linear improvement." (CEO Touya)
  • Versus the prior quarter’s transition-focused tone ("this is my final earnings call as CEO" (President, CEO & Executive Director Stephan Tanda, Q2 2026)), the current call carried more operational accountability language: "profitable growth, execution and disciplined capital allocation." (CEO Touya)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Leadership shifted from "my final earnings call as CEO" (President Tanda, Q2 2026) to "my first earnings call as CEO of Aptar." (CEO Touya)
  • The emergency medicine narrative stayed consistent quarter-to-quarter, but moved closer to resolution: "the year-over-year headwind will abate by the fourth quarter" (CFO Kanu, Q2 2026) versus "the destocking impact will be behind us" and "we've lapsed in Q4" (CEO Touya; CFO Kanu, Q3 2026).
  • Beauty discussion intensified around North America execution, building on earlier acknowledgment that Aptar "have fallen short in the Americas" (President Tanda, Q2 2026) to a more explicit transformation framing: "We have to do a transformation, and that's going to take time." (CEO Touya)

Risks and Concerns

  • "our Russian subsidiary... is now under administrative control" and "we have deconsolidated the Russian subsidiary" with the related deconsolidation charge described as excluded from adjusted earnings. (CFO Kanu)
  • "we do actually have some seasonality in 4Q" and "Q4 for the company is a seasonally softer quarter." (CFO Kanu)
  • "we are tracking and we are staying very closely connected to our customers" on cough/cold season demand variability. (CEO Touya)
  • "there's fundings into the ecosystem" but naloxone visibility was described as limited because "you cannot buy any IQVIA data or Nielsen type data, it doesn't exist." (CEO Touya)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized that Q3 delivered "5% core sales growth" and "adjusted earnings per share at the higher end of our guidance range" while setting expectations that emergency medicine destocking is expected to be "behind us" in Q4. The company’s near-term focus centered on Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of $1.39 to $1.47, continued capital investment plans, and shareholder returns through ongoing repurchases and a 4% dividend increase, alongside a stated push to bring "greater accountability and operational discipline" to Beauty’s North America margin recovery that was repeatedly characterized as not "a quick fix."

data.title: TFI forecasts Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.30-$1.40 amid focus on fixing U.S. LTL execution
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: TFI International (TFII) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Yesterday, after market close, TFI International reported another quarter of solid results with a standout performance from our Truckload segment." (President, CEO & Chairman Alain Bedard)

  • "Overall, adjusted diluted EPS was $1.67" and "we generated another $116 million of free cash flow, bringing our year-to-date total to more than $440 million." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "This very solid financial foundation allows us to thoughtfully invest for the future during up and down cycles alike and also allows us to return excess capital to shareholders whenever possible, which we did both during and subsequent to the third quarter." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "Truckload...had a phenomenal quarter" with "industry-leading adjusted OR of 86.7%" and results that "directly reflects our favorable exposure to the right end markets" and "our emphasis on the specialized side of the business." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "LTL was...$678 million" and "our adjusted OR was 91.3% and operating income was $44 million. Again, that's including a noncash impairment." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "Logistic also had a strong quarter" with "operating income jumped 59% to $49 million." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "We ended September with an adjusted funded debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 2.1" and "this is an updated measure, which excludes the letter of credit and contingent consideration." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "Our brokerage revenue in the quarter was up 49% year-over-year" and "it's like a hybrid business. It's not a pure asset-based business." (Chief Financial Officer David Saperstein)

Outlook

  • "Our updated outlook...includes fourth quarter adjusted EPS of $1.30 to $1.40." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "We continue to expect year-over-year adjusted operating ratio improvement of 400 to 500 basis points in the Truckload segment, 100 to 200 basis points for our Logistics and a slight decline maybe of 100 basis points up to 100 basis points for our LTL." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "We continue to expect net CapEx, excluding real estate, to be in the range of $225 million to $250 million." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • Guidance language on LTL risk was more explicit in Q3, with Bedard tying caution to U.S. LTL execution and a partnership change: "our 6 years partnership with our friend at UPS is coming to an end, okay, in early '27" and "this is why we're very careful about the guidance that we're giving for Q4." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

Financial Results

  • "Our top line total revenue before fuel surcharge of $1.9 billion was up 8%" and "overall operating income grew 17% to $180 million despite an office-related real estate impairment charge." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • "This was the second consecutive quarter that TFI International achieved a sub-90 operating ratio on a consolidated basis." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • Segment profitability mix emphasized Truckload and Logistics acceleration, as Bedard said Truckload operating income "nearly doubled" and Logistics operating income "was up 60%, almost 60%." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • LTL pressure centered on U.S. execution and network costs, with Saperstein pointing to the lag from actions taken during the quarter: "those costs came out of the network over the course of the quarter and not necessarily in lockstep with the volumes coming out." (Chief Financial Officer Saperstein)

Q&A

  • Ken Hoexter, BofA Securities: asked for deeper U.S. LTL detail and Q4 implications; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard said, "we've been going through a very rough patch in our U.S. LTL" and added, "our 6 years partnership with our friend at UPS is coming to an end...in early '27," linking it to guidance caution.

  • Scott Group, Wolfe Research: asked about U.S. LTL profitability and the UPS/GFP exposure; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard said, "you can think that our U.S. operation is more closer to a 97% OR" and clarified GFP: "that's going to come to an end at the end of January '27."

  • Uday Khanapurkar, TD Cowen: asked about U.S. LTL revenue per shipment/mix and linehaul pressures; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard said 3PL mix "is still a factor in Q3" and described linehaul sourcing: "about 55% of our miles is done through our own people...About 20-some percent is rail" and "we have to go on the spot market" when volume spiked.

  • Ravi Shanker, Morgan Stanley: asked about the LTL market and 2027 truckload upside; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard said, "the market is soft a bit. But price-wise...pricing is holding" and on truckload, "the market is still soft" but "the supply will stay constrained" if demand returns.

  • Walter Spracklin, RBC Capital Markets: asked about inflation and cost structure plus succession/alternatives; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard said truckload is seeing "some inflation on the salary" and in LTL "it's the third party that we're using...That is where we got a lot of cost increase"; on M&A capacity he said, "we've got capital to justify through debt $1 billion, $1.5 billion acquisition."

  • Jordan Alliger, Goldman Sachs: asked what’s driving Logistics and timing for U.S. LTL fix; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard said the change is "we're changing the recipe" and noted hiring: "this guy joined us October 1"; CFO Saperstein framed Logistics as "a collection of asset-light businesses" and said, "This is not just commoditized brokerage at all."

  • Cameron Doerksen, National Bank Financial: asked about divesting U.S. LTL; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard responded, "we have no intention of selling our U.S. LTL at all" and added, "the problem is the human."

  • Kevin Chiang, CIBC: asked about longer-term EPS power and buybacks; President, CEO & Chairman Bedard said, "we need the contribution of TForce Freight to be an $8 guy" and highlighted capital allocation tension: "Do you do M&A...Or do you just buy back your stock and wait."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to negative on U.S. LTL, repeatedly pressing on structural issues and alternatives, including divestiture and execution credibility; one prompt was, "what do you say to skeptics who say the business seems to be structurally broken." (Ariel Rosa, Citigroup)

  • Management tone was confident on Truckload and Logistics but defensive and frustrated on U.S. LTL, with Bedard saying, "it's like a broken story" and "I feel like I'm a broken record" while also asserting, "we know what to do." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • Versus Q2, management’s prepared remarks and Q&A in Q3 placed heavier emphasis on U.S. LTL problems and near-term disruption, particularly the UPS partnership ending, while continuing to describe Truckload as benefiting from "tightening capacity industry-wide" and a shift to specialized freight. (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 guidance shifted down sequentially, with Bedard guiding "fourth quarter adjusted EPS of $1.30 to $1.40" (Q3 call) versus Q2 guiding "third quarter...$1.70 to $1.80" (Q2 call, President, CEO & Chairman Bedard).

  • The tone on U.S. LTL moved from fixable pricing/cost actions in Q2 ("we have too much volume and not enough price" and "we just need to raise the price" (Chief Financial Officer Saperstein)) to a broader execution and culture reset in Q3 ("the problem is the people" and "we're changing the recipe" (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)).

  • New, time-specific overhang emerged in Q3 with Bedard’s disclosure: "our 6 years partnership...with UPS is coming to an end...at the end of January '27," which did not appear in the Q2 transcript. (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

Risks and Concerns

  • U.S. LTL execution risk remained central, with Bedard saying the business is "not performing well at all" and pointing to density and service issues: "our density is so bad" and "our service tanked." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • Customer/volume risk tied to UPS/GFP transition was flagged: "We anticipate that some customers will have to find a solution somewhere." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

  • Cost volatility risk was tied to third-party linehaul: "the spot market in Q2 and in Q3 for linehaul is just killing us" and later normalization: "at the end of Q3, we're back to normal because now...we don't have to go on the spot market." (President, CEO & Chairman Bedard)

Final Takeaway

TFI management described Q3 as a solid quarter led by Truckload and Logistics, with Bedard highlighting $1.67 adjusted EPS, $116 million of quarterly free cash flow, and an improved adjusted funded debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 2.1. The call’s main pressure point was U.S. LTL, where Bedard characterized performance as "a broken story," outlined a management and culture reset, and flagged a specific early-2027 change as the UPS reseller partnership ends, which he said contributed to being "very careful" with Q4 guidance of $1.30 to $1.40 in adjusted EPS.

data.title: Church & Dwight expects Q4 adjusted EPS to increase 17% to 19% as it raises 2026 organic sales growth outlook to ~5%
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Church & Dwight (CHD) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We delivered strong third quarter results" and "we exceeded our outlook across key metrics" while noting "conditions remain challenging, including inflationary pressure related to the Middle East conflict and increasing global transportation rates" (President, CEO & Director Richard Dierker).

  • "Net sales increased 1%, ahead of our outlook of a 1% decline" and "organic sales grew 5.1%, well above our 3% outlook" as "gross margin was... 46.8%, up 170 basis points, and adjusted EPS was $0.92... above our $0.89 outlook" (President, CEO & Director Dierker).

  • "THERABREATH continues to contribute considerably" with "record share level of 26.8%" and "WATERPIK... had double-digit sales growth"; by contrast, "TOUCHLAND sales growth in the U.S. has slowed from our original expectations" (President, CEO & Director Dierker).

  • "Revenues grew 20% in the quarter, and global online sales now represent 25.9% of total consumer sales" (President, CEO & Director Dierker).

  • "Third quarter adjusted EPS was $0.92... above our outlook" and "our third quarter gross margin increased to 46.8%" with "marketing investment levels reached 11.9% of sales" (CFO & Executive VP Lee McChesney).

  • "Our Board of Directors approved a new share repurchase program authorizing up to $1 billion of common stock repurchases" and "this program has no expiration date" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

Outlook

  • "We are raising our sales expectations and tightening our adjusted EPS outlook" and "for '26, we now expect organic sales growth of approximately 5%" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • "Our outlook for 2026 includes approximately $150 million of inflation" and "this outlook assumes roughly a crude oil price of $100 a barrel" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • "We now expect adjusted EPS of approximately 7%, tightening on our prior range of 6% to 8%" and "our cash from operations outlook remains approximately $1.175 billion" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • "If we turn to the fourth quarter, we expect organic sales growth of approximately 4% and adjusted EPS is expected to increase 17% to 19% versus last year" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s stance that "we are raising our full year organic sales outlook to approximately 4% to 5%" and "raising our adjusted EPS outlook to a growth rate of 6% to 8%" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney, Q2), Q3 moved to "approximately 5%" organic sales growth and an "approximately 7%" adjusted EPS growth expectation (CFO & Executive VP McChesney, Q3).

Financial Results

  • "Net sales increased 1%" and "organic sales grew 5.1%" with "volume growth of 4.6%" (President, CEO & Director Dierker).

  • "Third quarter adjusted EPS was $0.92" and "our third quarter gross margin increased to 46.8%" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • "Adjusted SG&A was $261 million or 16.3% of net sales" and "adjusted income from operations increased $27 million... to $298 million" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • "Cash from operations for the first 9 months of 2026 was $841 million" and "total debt was $2.2 billion and cash on hand was $447 million" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • "It was a net about $15 million in the third quarter" tariff refund impact, and "in the fourth quarter, we expect it to be about $5 million" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

Q&A

  • Anna Lizzul, BofA Securities: Asked about "innovation on the value tier" and "gross margin expansion into early 2027"; President, CEO & Director Dierker answered "we've gone through the ARM & HAMMER strategy... good, better, best" and said "you'll see some stuff coming in 2027," while CFO & Executive VP McChesney cited "record level of productivity in 2026" and said "we're optimistic for '27".

  • Peter Grom, UBS: Asked about category trends and why "4Q organic sales guidance" steps down; President, CEO & Director Dierker said categories are "closer to 2.5%" and on Q4 added "maybe we're being a little conservative" and "our trends are very strong as we look at October even".

  • Bonnie Herzog, Goldman Sachs: Asked about commodity hedging and pricing/promo intensity; President, CEO & Director Dierker said "the consumer is still stretched" and described laundry deal levels rising "to around 40%" while CFO & Executive VP McChesney said the company is "slightly hedged a bit more than we were at this time last year".

  • Rupesh Parikh, Oppenheimer: Asked about HERO internationally and TOUCHLAND’s outlook; President, CEO & Director Dierker said HERO is "definitely a net sales driver" internationally and for TOUCHLAND said "the business is going to be close to flattish all in" with "growth in 2027" expected.

  • Christopher Carey, Wells Fargo: Asked tariff refund benefit and THERABREATH durability; CFO & Executive VP McChesney said "net about $15 million" in Q3 and "about $5 million" in Q4, while President, CEO & Director Dierker said THERABREATH is "growing double digits" and "our repeat rate is fantastic" and added toothpaste repeat rate is "closing in on 30%".

  • Nik Modi, RBC: Asked about operating leverage and TOUCHLAND placement; President, CEO & Director Dierker said "you should expect some leverage" and on TOUCHLAND said distribution will be "in a couple of different classes of trade" and confirmed "that's where we expect it to be" when asked about "beauty and mass".

  • Andrea Teixeira, JPMorgan: Pressed on pricing into 2027; President, CEO & Director Dierker said "I'm not going to make any more comments on pricing than what I've already made" and reiterated "first and foremost, we focus on productivity" and "our goal each and every year is to expand margin".

  • Olivia Tong Cheang, Raymond James: Asked what top-line drivers are repeatable and international price/mix; President, CEO & Director Dierker said "our growth isn't just one brand, it's broad-based" and previewed "I'm going to announce in January the category that we're going to go into in the U.S. for ARM & HAMMER" and added on international M&A "we're looking at acquisitions all the time outside the U.S.".

  • Kaumil Gajrawala, Jefferies: Asked buyback intent vs M&A and 2027 gross margin targets; President, CEO & Director Dierker called the buyback "more housekeeping" and on margins said "not ready to put that out there yet" and "feel free" to ask again in January.

  • Lauren Lieberman, Barclays: Questioned net sales guidance implications and MISS MOUTH’S trends; President, CEO & Director Dierker said "maybe we're a little conservative" on Q4 and CFO & Executive VP McChesney said "MISS MOUTH'S is off to a great start".

  • Stephen Robert Powers, Deutsche Bank: Asked WTI vs Brent and TOUCHLAND trajectory; CFO & Executive VP McChesney said "$100 oil... would be WTI" and President, CEO & Director Dierker said TOUCHLAND is "flattish" for the year and cited retailer resets where "the set is absolutely beautiful".

  • Filippo Falorni, Citi: Asked inflation mix and transport as structural plus international M&A criteria; CFO & Executive VP McChesney said the inflation increase was "a mix of commodities and a mix of transportation" and linked transport to "a shortage of drivers," while President, CEO & Director Dierker said M&A criteria remain "#1, #2 brand" and "gross margin accretive, asset-light" with "a little bit more latitude" internationally.

  • Edward Lewis, Rothschild & Co Redburn: Asked whether e-commerce exposure is an advantage; President, CEO & Director Dierker said "partially, yes" and cited portfolio mix where acquisitions like "TOUCHLAND, MISS MOUTH" "are over-indexed to online".

  • Sergio Matsumoto, TD Cowen (for Rob Moskow): Asked about licensing/incubator reacquisitions; President, CEO & Director Dierker said "there's one that we've already taken back" and "there's 2 or 3 that we're looking at" with more to come at Analyst Day.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical on forward margins, pricing, and guidance mechanics, including direct challenges such as "how we should start thinking about gross margin expansion into early 2027" (Anna Lizzul, BofA), "how hedged are you" (Bonnie Herzog, Goldman Sachs), and pricing pressure requests where "I was wondering if you can comment" on 2027 positioning (Andrea Teixeira, JPMorgan).

  • Management’s prepared-remarks tone was positive and confident, anchored by statements such as "We delivered strong third quarter results" and "we remain confident" (President, CEO & Director Dierker) and "we are very pleased" and "remain confident" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • In Q&A, management mixed confidence with select restraint, including "we're optimistic for '27" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney) but also boundary-setting like "I'm not going to make any more comments on pricing" (President, CEO & Director Dierker) and deferrals such as "I'll give you more of an update at our Analyst Day" (President, CEO & Director Dierker).

  • Versus Q2’s more upbeat macro framing that "consumer spending remains resilient" (President, CEO & Director Dierker, Q2), Q3’s opening leaned more cautious on the environment, stating "conditions remain challenging" with elevated "inflationary pressure" and "transportation rates" (President, CEO & Director Dierker, Q3).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The inflation and oil language shifted from "approximately $30 million" of cost pressure and "approximately $90 a barrel" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney, Q2) to "approximately $150 million of inflation" and "$100 a barrel" in Q3 (CFO & Executive VP McChesney, Q3).

  • Q2 positioned TOUCHLAND as still growing with "we expect continued sales growth in the second half of the year" (President, CEO & Director Dierker, Q2), while Q3 reset expectations to "close to flattish all in" for the year, paired with plans that "we expect growth in 2027" (President, CEO & Director Dierker, Q3).

  • Q3 introduced new capital return capacity, as "a new share repurchase program authorizing up to $1 billion" replaced the prior authorization (CFO & Executive VP McChesney), while Q2 did not highlight a new repurchase authorization.

  • Both quarters emphasized the same strategic pillars, but Q3 elevated the timeline specificity, including "our Analyst Day at the end of January" and "first formal update" on "2030 growth initiatives" (President, CEO & Director Dierker).

Risks and Concerns

  • "Inflationary pressure related to the Middle East conflict and increasing global transportation rates" were cited as ongoing headwinds (President, CEO & Director Dierker), with mitigation described as "delivering incremental productivity" and using "our RGM toolkit" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • Management flagged a larger cost backdrop, stating "our outlook for 2026 includes approximately $150 million of inflation" and noting both commodity and freight dynamics, while also saying teams have "helped our business deliver gross margin improvements every quarter in 2026" (CFO & Executive VP McChesney).

  • Brand-specific risk centered on TOUCHLAND’s near-term slowdown, with management stating U.S. growth "has slowed from our original expectations" due to "competitive products growing in channels that we did not compete in" (President, CEO & Director Dierker), alongside mitigation through distribution expansion and international rollout.

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as an “exceeded our outlook” quarter driven by volume-led organic growth and gross margin expansion, while raising 2026 organic sales expectations to approximately 5% and tightening adjusted EPS growth to approximately 7%. The company highlighted increased inflation and transportation pressures tied to the Middle East conflict and higher freight rates, but emphasized productivity, RGM actions, and marketing investment as offsets. Investor focus in Q&A clustered around the durability of THERABREATH, the reset in TOUCHLAND’s near-term trajectory, the path for margins into 2027 under higher input costs, and the implications of a new $1B share repurchase authorization, with management repeatedly pointing to additional detail at the late-January Analyst Day.

data.title: Sandisk slides 13% on post-earnings selloff
data.description:
Shares of Sandisk Corporation (SNDK), a standalone NAND flash memory and storage company, sank more than 13% on Friday after the firm's fiscal first-quarter earnings report.

The stock closed at $1,150.89, down $179.16 on the day. Investors weighed strong datacenter demand and a surprise stock split against lingering concerns over consumer weakness and competitive pressures in the memory market.

What Happened to Sandisk

The session's decline followed Sandisk's fiscal first-quarter earnings release on October 29, which showed results and guidance above analyst estimates. The company reported non-GAAP diluted earnings of $49.51 per share and revenue of $11.03 billion for the quarter, beating consensus estimates.

For the second quarter, management guided revenue to a range of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion and non-GAAP earnings to $55 to $57 per share on a pre-split basis.

Along with the results, Sandisk's board approved an 8-for-1 forward stock split. Shareholders of record on November 9, 2026 are set to receive seven additional shares for each share held, with split-adjusted trading expected to begin on November 20, 2026.

On the earnings call, management emphasized AI-driven NAND demand, datacenter mix expansion, and the growing adoption of New Business Model agreements as the predominant way Sandisk works with customers. The company also pointed to substantial adjusted free cash flow generated in the quarter.

On the negative side, management acknowledged that consumer revenue declined sequentially as customers adjusted to higher pricing, while wafer production lead times limit the company's ability to reallocate supply quickly.

data.title: American Savings Bank signals NIM expansion as it expects one Fed rate hike in Q4 2026
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: American Savings Bank (ASBH) Q3 2026

Management View

  • “We appreciate you joining us for our first earnings call as a public company.” (President, CEO & Director Ann Teranishi)
  • “We delivered another quarter of strong earnings with net income of $29 million or $0.45 per diluted share, return on average assets of 1.29% and a return on average tangible common equity of 16.68%.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Average loan balances increased and deposit costs decreased despite a rising rate environment.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Local economists continue to forecast growth in 2026, but have recently lowered their estimates.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Net interest income was $76.4 million, up $1.2 million from the prior quarter... Net interest margin was 3.61%, 4 basis points higher than the prior quarter and 15 basis points higher than the prior year period.” (Executive VP & CFO Dane Teruya)
  • “With our ability to generate capital and our focus on returning capital to shareholders, the Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.27 per common share payable on November 20 to shareholders of record as of November 9.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Nonperforming loans were 29 basis points of total loans compared with 19 basis points in the prior quarter... net charge-offs were $1.8 million or 11 basis points on an annualized basis.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Steven Nakahara)

Outlook

  • “What you'll see is it slightly ticking up in the fourth quarter, but relatively only about a couple of basis points up.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Right now, we're expecting one [rate hike] in the fourth quarter. There is also probably a couple that will occur in 2027... we would expect our cost of funds to inch higher as those rate changes become effective.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Our balance sheet continues to be neutral to slightly asset sensitive, which will support NIM expansion in this higher for longer interest rate environment.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “For this year, we think that the effective tax rate will be closer to 22%... the tax rate in the mid-22s to 23% level is an appropriate level going forward.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “With this rate environment, we are expecting the residential portfolio to stay flat... production will really offset the runoff.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)

Financial Results

  • “Net income for the third quarter was $29 million, an increase of $1.8 million or 6.7% from the prior quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Noninterest income was $21 million, down $2.8 million from the prior quarter, primarily due to lower fair market value adjustments related to our BOLI portfolio.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Noninterest expense was $59 million, down $2.1 million from the prior quarter, primarily due to lower fair market value adjustment related to our deferred compensation plan.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Total assets were $8.9 billion at quarter end, down $112.2 million or 1.2% from June 30.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Total deposits ended the quarter at $8.1 billion, down $137.6 million or 1.7% from the prior quarter... Noninterest-bearing deposits made up 31.5% of total deposits.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Our Tier 1 leverage ratio increased to 9.24% and our total capital ratio increased to 14.76%.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “The allowance for credit losses on loans was $60.2 million at quarter end or 97 basis points of total loans... Provision expense was $0.7 million in the third quarter, down $2.6 million from the linked quarter.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara)

Q&A

  • Jeff Rulis, D.A. Davidson: asked about deposit-cost pressure and margin trajectory; Executive VP & CFO Teruya replied, “what you'll see is it slightly ticking up in the fourth quarter... only about a couple of basis points up,” and added, “we would expect our cost of funds to inch higher as those rate changes become effective.”
  • Jeff Rulis, D.A. Davidson: asked about the expense run-rate excluding one-time fair value items; Executive VP & CFO Teruya said, “if you eliminate the fair market value related to our deferred comp plans, we think the -- that would be a good run rate for the fourth quarter,” and noted “some inflationary impacts on that number.”
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked about reinvestment opportunities from single-family runoff and securities cash flows; Executive VP & CFO Teruya said, “The cash flow that came off in the third quarter was roughly about $55 million,” and added, “we got roughly about $74 million runoff... reinvesting... at a spread of a little more than 175 basis points.”
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked about CD runoff and new CD duration; Executive VP & CFO Teruya responded, “our customers' demand is going to be a little shorter... promotional campaigns in the 3-month and 6-month range,” and said, “we think that trend will continue, but eventually will stabilize.”
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked about timing for a buyback; Executive VP & CFO Teruya replied, “we haven't made any determination on what we're going to be doing with that excess capital, but we're having active discussions.”
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: asked about deposit outflows and early Q4 trends; Executive VP & CFO Teruya answered, “The deposit outflow in the third quarter was seasonal,” and added, “we do expect a pickup in the fourth quarter.”
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: asked about the nonaccrual increase and interest income impact; Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara said, “The increase in nonaccrual was associated with the partial charge-off of the same CRE construction deal,” and added, “no material change on the interest income.”
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: asked about the go-forward tax rate; Executive VP & CFO Teruya said, “the tax rate in the mid-22s to 23% level is an appropriate level going forward.”
  • Kelly Motta, KBW: asked about the loan pipeline and growth outlook; President, CEO & Director Teranishi replied, “The pipeline is looking pretty steady and healthy, not as robust as earlier this year,” and added, “we're really being disciplined in our approach on credit as well as pricing.”
  • Kelly Motta, KBW: asked about momentum in noninterest-bearing deposits; President, CEO & Director Teranishi said, “we continue to have a terrific steady deposit base,” while Executive VP & CFO Teruya added, “We're really trying to build primary banking relationships.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was neutral to slightly skeptical, concentrated on rate sensitivity, deposit behavior, expense run-rate, and capital return, including buyback timing.
  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and largely steady in Q&A, emphasizing consistency and discipline, including “Our balance sheet continues to be neutral to slightly asset sensitive” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya) and “we're really being disciplined in our approach on credit as well as pricing” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi).
  • A prior-quarter transcript was not provided, so tone changes versus last quarter were not discussed on this call.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The previous-quarter transcript was not available in the provided materials, so changes in strategy, guidance language, and tone versus last quarter could not be directly assessed.

Risks and Concerns

  • “Local economists continue to forecast growth in 2026, but have recently lowered their estimates.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Hawaii faces elevated oil prices and impacts from recent storms.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “In the third quarter, we recognized a partial charge-off of a nonperforming commercial construction loan.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara)
  • “Nonperforming loans were 29 basis points of total loans compared with 19 basis points in the prior quarter.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara)

Final Takeaway

American Savings Bank framed Q3 as a strong quarter marked by net income of $29 million and modest net interest margin expansion, while management highlighted a low deposit-cost profile and a “neutral to slightly asset sensitive” balance sheet positioned for incremental NIM improvement in a “higher for longer” rate backdrop. In Q&A, management’s near-term focus centered on limited deposit-rate pressure (“only about a couple of basis points”), seasonal deposit flows expected to reverse in Q4, disciplined loan growth with a flatter residential outlook, and ongoing Board discussions about optimizing capital beyond the newly declared $0.27 quarterly dividend, alongside continued monitoring of credit performance following a partial charge-off that lifted nonaccruals.
